name: Clip Export
author: zysilm
punchline: Cut part of a video into a new file: a lossless stream copy, a re-encoded MP4, or an animated GIF or WebP
description:
Exports part of the local video playing as a new file, from a sidebar tab, Clip Export. Fast copies the streams (lossless, about as fast as the disk, from the keyframe at or before the start); Precise re-encodes an MP4 from the exact frame, with a quality preset or your own settings, and can include the video effects and burned-in subtitles; its Animated GIF and Animated WebP presets write a small looping image instead (up to 60 seconds). Set the range by typing it, with Now, from the A-B loop, or export the last 10–120 seconds with one key. The range shows on the seek bar while the tab is open; running exports show their progress, and the last twenty clips stay in Results.
The Collection page gathers ranges from several local files into one list: reorder it, remove parts, preview a part with a double click, and export them as one merged video (Fast when the files match, Precise otherwise).
The Highlights page finds the moments of a video that stand out by their loudness (stand-up, talk shows, streams, sports): press Find Highlights, look through the suggested ranges (each starts at the pause before its moment) and add them to the Collection. The scan runs on this computer, only when you ask for it, and is kept per file.
Video ▸ Export Clip… opens the tab.
